meta.title: Consistent Company Voice
meta.description: Model specialization: Claude orchestrates, Codex shapes the client-facing voice.

slides.title: The problem
slides.body:
Everything I put in front of a client —
proposals, service pages, the website —
needs to sound like the same company.

Consistent voice.

slides.title: The scale
slides.body:
By the time I'm ready to write,
my workspace has over 1,200 markdown files —
research, competitor analysis, pricing data,
earlier drafts.

Some of that research ran
independently for five or six hours.

slides.title: Claude orchestrates
slides.body:
Claude navigates through all of it —
pulling the right context
to help shape the document.

I work through it interactively.
Many rounds, many changes.
This part isn't automatic.

slides.title: Codex shapes the voice
slides.body:
Then Codex reviews the client-facing text.
Sometimes Gemini too.

Not just grammar.
The voice, the tone, how it reads
to someone deciding whether
to work with me.

slides.title: Same loop, every surface
slides.body:
Proposals.
Service pages.
The website.

One consistent voice,
checked by a model that writes
better for clients than the one
that researched and structured it.

slides.title:
Each model does
what it's genuinely better at.
Not interchangeably.
slides.body:
dispatch is the open-source plugin
I use for this — link's in the first comment.
